graph.title: Arduino MKR1000 Audio Input (Analog to MIDI frequency meter)

parts.label: MKR1000 VCC to top power rail

notes: Parts are unchanged from step 1, except that the board's type changed. The catalogue's arduino-mkr1000 card has no analog or digital pins (only USB, VIN, VCC, GND, BAT), so the A0 wire could not be attached. The board is now the new type arduino-mkr1000-headers (MKR1000 with pin headers, ports A0-A6, D0-D14, VCC, GND and others), modelled on the existing arduino-yun-headers entry. It is still the same physical MKR1000 board.

Breadboard hole names follow the catalogue: rows a-e are bank 't', rows f-j are bank 'b'. In the image rows A-E are drawn at the bottom half, and the rails are tp (top, red row), bn (bottom, blue/negative row).
The LMV358 has its notch at the left. Pins 1-4 (OUT1, IN1-, IN1+, GND) are in 14-17t.e, and pins 5-8 (IN2+, IN2-, OUT2, VCC) are in 17-14b.f.

Net list built from the image and schematic. VCC feeds R8 (100k) to the + input, which is biased to mid-supply. R9 (100k) goes from the + input to GND. C1 (100n) couples the jack signal to the + input. R10 (47k) goes from the - input to GND. R11 (47k) goes to the trimmer end, and the trimmer wiper goes to the op-amp output (non-inverting gain stage).

In the image the brown wire from the MKR1000 A0 pin lands on the op-amp pin 1 (OUT1) column, so A0 is wired to OUT1. This is as the image shows. The schematic's DAC0/A0 comes from the second amplifier, whose inputs are left unconnected there.

The trimmer is placed in 1-3t.e, with the wiper on column 2 and the end pin on column 3 (R11). The purple wire goes from 2t.d to op-amp OUT1. In the image the purple wire starts in the top-half column 2, but only this placement makes the wiper connection electrically work.
Jack ports: SLEEVE goes to GND and RING1 (right channel) goes through C1 to the amplifier. The wires from the jack are treated as soldered to the breakout pins.
The MKR1000 is powered over USB. No USB cable is in the parts list or image, so none is added.

The resistor leads were read as 4 holes apart. R8 is 12-16, R9 is 16-20, R11 is 3-7 and R10 is 6-10. The resistor colour bands were hard to read, so values are taken from the parts list and schematic.
